source_evidence: Unlike traditional mutual funds (or “open-end funds”), they are not required to buy back shares from shareholders. After that, their shares trade on national securities exchanges at market prices.
answer: Publicly traded closed-end funds sell shares in a public offering, and afterward those shares trade on national securities exchanges. Investors may buy or sell shares there at market prices, which can be higher or lower than the value of the fund’s underlying investments. This exchange trading is different from redeeming shares with the fund: a publicly traded closed-end fund is not required to buy back shares from its shareholders.
